    End to end — summer NDVI over Lake Tahoe¶

    You turn a Sentinel-2 search into an NDVI map of Lake Tahoe in about thirty lines. This notebook owns step 1 of a three-part story, find, and runs the other two steps briefly. The patcher notebook goes deeper on cut, the operators notebook on compute.

    Setting Value
    AOI Lake Tahoe, lon/lat (-120.25, 38.85, -119.85, 39.30)
    Season 2024-06-01 to 2024-09-30
    Archive Sentinel-2 L2A on the Microsoft Planetary Computer
    Bands red B04 and near-infrared B08

    What you'll learn:

    1. Turn a STAC search into a queryable catalog with gc.sources.from_stac_search.
    2. Filter it by space, time and cloud cover with query and where.
    3. Pick the clearest date that covers the whole AOI.
    4. Stage the files and build a patcher field with gc.patch.field_for.
    5. Tile, compute NDVI and stitch with geotoolz.patch_ops.

    1. Discover — a STAC search becomes a catalog¶

    gc.sources.from_stac_search runs the search and returns one catalog row per (item, asset). asset_key="*" keeps every asset, so later steps can pick bands. extra_properties copies eo:cloud_cover into a column you can filter on.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    BBOX: tuple[float, float, float, float] = (-120.25, 38.85, -119.85, 39.30)  # lon/lat
SEASON: str = "2024-06-01/2024-09-30"

client: pystac_client.Client = pystac_client.Client.open(
    "https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1",
    modifier=planetary_computer.sign_inplace,  # signed hrefs, so rasterio can read them
)
catalog: gc.GeoCatalog = gc.sources.from_stac_search(
    client,
    collections=["sentinel-2-l2a"],
    bounds=BBOX,
    datetime=SEASON,
    asset_key="*",
    extra_properties=("eo:cloud_cover",),
)
print(f"{len(catalog)} (item, asset) rows")
print(f"temporal extent: {catalog.temporal_extent}")
catalog.gdf[["asset_key", "stac_item_id", "crs", "eo:cloud_cover"]].head()

    2. Filter — space, time, cloud cover and bands¶

    A GeoSlice is the request every catalog answers: bounds, time interval, resolution and CRS. query filters by space and time; where filters on any other column with a pandas query string. See Catalog concepts for the GeoSlice contract.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    aoi: gc.GeoSlice = gc.GeoSlice(
    bounds=BBOX,
    interval=pd.Interval(
        pd.Timestamp("2024-06-01"), pd.Timestamp("2024-09-30"), closed="both"
    ),
    resolution=(3e-4, 3e-4),  # ≈ 30 m, a 3× decimation of the native 10 m grid
    crs="EPSG:4326",
)
hits: gc.GeoCatalog = catalog.query(aoi).where(
    "`eo:cloud_cover` < 20 and asset_key in ['B04', 'B08']"
)
print(f"{len(hits)} rows: red + NIR, under 20 % cloud")
    aoi: gc.GeoSlice = gc.GeoSlice( bounds=BBOX, interval=pd.Interval( pd.Timestamp("2024-06-01"), pd.Timestamp("2024-09-30"), closed="both" ), resolution=(3e-4, 3e-4), # ≈ 30 m, a 3× decimation of the native 10 m grid crs="EPSG:4326", ) hits: gc.GeoCatalog = catalog.query(aoi).where( "`eo:cloud_cover` < 20 and asset_key in ['B04', 'B08']" ) print(f"{len(hits)} rows: red + NIR, under 20 % cloud")
    162 rows: red + NIR, under 20 % cloud

    3. Choose — the clearest date that covers the whole AOI¶

    Lake Tahoe sits where UTM zones 10 and 11 meet, so each date brings two or more tiles. The lowest-cloud tile is not enough: some tiles are mostly no-data, and a 0 % cloud cover over no pixels is useless.

    Each footprint traces a tile's valid data. Group the rows by date, keep the dates whose footprints cover the AOI, and take the clearest.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    aoi_box: shapely.Polygon = shapely.box(*BBOX)
table: pd.DataFrame = hits.gdf.assign(date=hits.gdf.index.left.date)
lowest: pd.Series = table.sort_values("eo:cloud_cover").iloc[0]
share: float = lowest.geometry.intersection(aoi_box).area / aoi_box.area
print(f"lowest-cloud tile {lowest['stac_item_id']} covers {share:.1%} of the AOI")
per_day: pd.DataFrame = table.groupby("date").agg(
    cloud_cover=("eo:cloud_cover", "max"),
    coverage=(
        "geometry",
        lambda g: shapely.union_all(g.values).intersection(aoi_box).area / aoi_box.area,
    ),
    tiles=("stac_item_id", "nunique"),
)
full: pd.DataFrame = per_day[per_day["coverage"] > 0.999]
best_day: dt.date = full["cloud_cover"].idxmin()
print(f"{len(full)} of {len(per_day)} dates cover the AOI; clearest: {best_day}")
full.sort_values("cloud_cover").head()
    aoi_box: shapely.Polygon = shapely.box(*BBOX) table: pd.DataFrame = hits.gdf.assign(date=hits.gdf.index.left.date) lowest: pd.Series = table.sort_values("eo:cloud_cover").iloc[0] share: float = lowest.geometry.intersection(aoi_box).area / aoi_box.area print(f"lowest-cloud tile {lowest['stac_item_id']} covers {share:.1%} of the AOI") per_day: pd.DataFrame = table.groupby("date").agg( cloud_cover=("eo:cloud_cover", "max"), coverage=( "geometry", lambda g: shapely.union_all(g.values).intersection(aoi_box).area / aoi_box.area, ), tiles=("stac_item_id", "nunique"), ) full: pd.DataFrame = per_day[per_day["coverage"] > 0.999] best_day: dt.date = full["cloud_cover"].idxmin() print(f"{len(full)} of {len(per_day)} dates cover the AOI; clearest: {best_day}") full.sort_values("cloud_cover").head()
    lowest-cloud tile S2B_MSIL2A_20240806T184919_R113_T11SKD_20240806T235408 covers 0.0% of the AOI

    4. Stage and load — local files, then a patcher field¶

    gc.staging.stage downloads each row's file once into a local cache and returns a catalog that points at the copies. gc.patch.field_for mosaics them onto the slice grid and wraps the result as a gp.RasterField. Both tiles are reprojected onto the slice's lon/lat grid on the way in.

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    start: pd.Timestamp = pd.Timestamp(best_day)
end: pd.Timestamp = start + pd.Timedelta(hours=23, minutes=59)
day: gc.GeoSlice = gc.GeoSlice(
    bounds=BBOX,
    interval=pd.Interval(start, end, closed="both"),
    resolution=aoi.resolution,
    crs=aoi.crs,
)
cache: Path = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "geotoolz-tahoe"  # reused across runs
rows: gc.GeoCatalog = hits.query(day)
red_rows: gc.GeoCatalog = gc.staging.stage(rows.where("asset_key == 'B04'"), dest=cache)
nir_rows: gc.GeoCatalog = gc.staging.stage(rows.where("asset_key == 'B08'"), dest=cache)
red: gp.RasterField = gc.patch.field_for(red_rows, day)  # (1, 1500, 1333) uint16
nir: gp.RasterField = gc.patch.field_for(nir_rows, day)  # (1, 1500, 1333) uint16
scene: GeoTensor = gz.StackBands()([red.reader, nir.reader])  # (2, 1500, 1333) uint16
print(
    f"scene: {scene.shape} {scene.dtype}, crs={scene.crs}, fill={scene.fill_value_default}"
)
    start: pd.Timestamp = pd.Timestamp(best_day) end: pd.Timestamp = start + pd.Timedelta(hours=23, minutes=59) day: gc.GeoSlice = gc.GeoSlice( bounds=BBOX, interval=pd.Interval(start, end, closed="both"), resolution=aoi.resolution, crs=aoi.crs, ) cache: Path = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "geotoolz-tahoe" # reused across runs rows: gc.GeoCatalog = hits.query(day) red_rows: gc.GeoCatalog = gc.staging.stage(rows.where("asset_key == 'B04'"), dest=cache) nir_rows: gc.GeoCatalog = gc.staging.stage(rows.where("asset_key == 'B08'"), dest=cache) red: gp.RasterField = gc.patch.field_for(red_rows, day) # (1, 1500, 1333) uint16 nir: gp.RasterField = gc.patch.field_for(nir_rows, day) # (1, 1500, 1333) uint16 scene: GeoTensor = gz.StackBands()([red.reader, nir.reader]) # (2, 1500, 1333) uint16 print( f"scene: {scene.shape} {scene.dtype}, crs={scene.crs}, fill={scene.fill_value_default}" )
    scene: (2, 1500, 1333) uint16, crs=EPSG:4326, fill=0.0

    5. Cut and compute — NDVI tile by tile¶

    Three patch_ops operators put the patcher inside a Sequential: split the field, run an operator on every chip, stitch the chips back. The chip operator is gz.DNToReflectance (Sentinel-2 L2A stores reflectance × 10 000) followed by gz.NDVI. The cut and compute notebooks explain each half.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    patcher: gp.SpatialPatcher = gp.SpatialPatcher(
    geometry=gp.spatial.geometry.Rectangular(size=(256, 256), boundary="pad"),
    sampler=gp.spatial.sampler.RegularStride(step=(192, 192)),  # 64 px overlap
    window=gp.spatial.window.Hann(),
    aggregation=gp.spatial.aggregation.OverlapAdd(),
)
ndvi_op: gz.Sequential = gz.DNToReflectance(scale=1e-4) | gz.NDVI(red=0, nir=1)
field: gp.RasterField = gp.RasterField(scene)
tiled: gz.Sequential = gz.Sequential(
    [
        GridSampler(patcher=patcher),  # field → list[Patch]
        ApplyToChips(operator=ndvi_op),  # (2, 256, 256) uint16 → (256, 256) float64
        MergePatches(aggregation=patcher.aggregation, domain=field.domain),
    ]
)
ndvi: GeoTensor = tiled(field)  # (2, 1500, 1333) uint16 → (1500, 1333) float64
print(f"{patcher.n_anchors(field)} chips → ndvi {ndvi.shape} {ndvi.dtype}")
print(f"NDVI range: [{np.nanmin(ndvi):.2f}, {np.nanmax(ndvi):.2f}]")
    patcher: gp.SpatialPatcher = gp.SpatialPatcher( geometry=gp.spatial.geometry.Rectangular(size=(256, 256), boundary="pad"), sampler=gp.spatial.sampler.RegularStride(step=(192, 192)), # 64 px overlap window=gp.spatial.window.Hann(), aggregation=gp.spatial.aggregation.OverlapAdd(), ) ndvi_op: gz.Sequential = gz.DNToReflectance(scale=1e-4) | gz.NDVI(red=0, nir=1) field: gp.RasterField = gp.RasterField(scene) tiled: gz.Sequential = gz.Sequential( [ GridSampler(patcher=patcher), # field → list[Patch] ApplyToChips(operator=ndvi_op), # (2, 256, 256) uint16 → (256, 256) float64 MergePatches(aggregation=patcher.aggregation, domain=field.domain), ] ) ndvi: GeoTensor = tiled(field) # (2, 1500, 1333) uint16 → (1500, 1333) float64 print(f"{patcher.n_anchors(field)} chips → ndvi {ndvi.shape} {ndvi.dtype}") print(f"NDVI range: [{np.nanmin(ndvi):.2f}, {np.nanmax(ndvi):.2f}]")
    56 chips → ndvi (1500, 1333) float64
NDVI range: [-0.23, 0.71]

    NDVI is a per-pixel index, so the tiled result matches NDVI of the whole scene. The only difference is a one-pixel ring on the top and left edges, where the Hann window has zero weight (see Window convention).

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    whole: GeoTensor = ndvi_op(scene)  # (2, 1500, 1333) uint16 → (1500, 1333) float64
tiled_px: np.ndarray = np.asarray(ndvi)[1:, 1:]  # (1499, 1332) float64
whole_px: np.ndarray = np.asarray(whole)[1:, 1:]  # (1499, 1332) float64
print(
    f"max |tiled − whole| inside the border ring: {np.nanmax(np.abs(tiled_px - whole_px)):.1e}"
)
    whole: GeoTensor = ndvi_op(scene) # (2, 1500, 1333) uint16 → (1500, 1333) float64 tiled_px: np.ndarray = np.asarray(ndvi)[1:, 1:] # (1499, 1332) float64 whole_px: np.ndarray = np.asarray(whole)[1:, 1:] # (1499, 1332) float64 print( f"max |tiled − whole| inside the border ring: {np.nanmax(np.abs(tiled_px - whole_px)):.1e}" )
    max |tiled − whole| inside the border ring: 2.2e-16
    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    extent: tuple[float, float, float, float] = (BBOX[0], BBOX[2], BBOX[1], BBOX[3])
fig, (ax_red, ax_ndvi) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5))
ax_red.imshow(np.asarray(scene)[0], cmap="Greys_r", vmin=0, vmax=3000, extent=extent)
ax_red.set_title(f"Red (B04) DN, {best_day}")
im = ax_ndvi.imshow(np.asarray(ndvi), cmap="RdYlGn", vmin=-0.2, vmax=0.8, extent=extent)
ax_ndvi.set_title("NDVI, tiled and stitched")
fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax_ndvi, label="NDVI")
for ax in (ax_red, ax_ndvi):
    ax.set_xlabel("lon")
    ax.set_ylabel("lat")
plt.show()
    extent: tuple[float, float, float, float] = (BBOX[0], BBOX[2], BBOX[1], BBOX[3]) fig, (ax_red, ax_ndvi) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5)) ax_red.imshow(np.asarray(scene)[0], cmap="Greys_r", vmin=0, vmax=3000, extent=extent) ax_red.set_title(f"Red (B04) DN, {best_day}") im = ax_ndvi.imshow(np.asarray(ndvi), cmap="RdYlGn", vmin=-0.2, vmax=0.8, extent=extent) ax_ndvi.set_title("NDVI, tiled and stitched") fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax_ndvi, label="NDVI") for ax in (ax_red, ax_ndvi): ax.set_xlabel("lon") ax.set_ylabel("lat") plt.show()

    Forest around the lake reads green, the lake and bare granite read red. Fallen Leaf Lake is the small water body south-west of the lake.

    Summary¶

    • from_stac_search turned a STAC search into a catalog you can query and filter with where.
    • Footprints and cloud cover picked one clear date that covers the whole AOI.
    • stage and field_for turned that date's rows into a RasterField on your grid.
    • GridSampler → ApplyToChips → MergePatches computed NDVI tile by tile.

    Next: cut the same scene into patches and see why the window matters, or compute a cloud-masked NDVI with a Graph. To keep the catalog between sessions, write it with gc.storage.to_geoparquet; see From STAC.
